title: LGBTQ Federal Employees Targeted in DEI Purge and Firings
synopsis: Beginning January 20, 2025, Trump's executive orders on DEI and 'gender ideology' immediately placed employees whose roles involved 'promoting gender ideology' on paid administrative leave with computer access cut off, and at least six EOs directly targeted LGBTQ people in the federal workforce. The Williams Institute estimated approximately 314,000 LGBTQ employees of the federal government, USPS, and federal contractors were exposed to displacement. An OPM memo in early February directed agencies to prohibit employee resource groups promoting 'DEIA initiatives,' and OPM opened a tipline for workers to report colleagues involved in DEI activities — drawing comparisons to the 1950s 'Lavender Scare.' Trump also rescinded a nearly 60-year-old executive order (EO 11246) on January 21, 2025 prohibiting discrimination by federal contractors, removing protections for roughly 100,000 LGBTQ contractor employees. The Department of Homeland Security announced it would allow its agents to conduct surveillance based solely on a target's gender identity or sexual orientation. On March 26, 2025, a class-action complaint was filed before the Merit Systems Protection Board on behalf of fired federal DEI employees.

title: State-Level Anti-Trans Surge: 600+ Bills Follow Federal Lead
synopsis: In 2025, the ACLU documented more than 600 anti-transgender bills introduced at the U.S. state level — a new record, exceeding the 500-plus bills introduced in both 2023 and 2024 — directly emboldened by Trump's federal executive orders on sex definitions and gender-affirming care. By December 2025, 29 states had enacted at least one law restricting transgender youth healthcare, sports participation, bathroom access, or pronoun use in schools, and 348,400 transgender youth aged 13–17 lived in states that had banned them from bathrooms aligned with their gender identity. Twelve states enacted new bathroom bans in 2025 alone — including Georgia, Montana, Texas, and Wyoming. The Supreme Court's June 2025 ruling in U.S. v. Skrmetti upheld Tennessee's healthcare ban under the Equal Protection Clause, removing the primary constitutional barrier to state bans and triggering immediate enforcement in multiple states. By August 2025, at least eight major hospital systems in Democratic-led states had halted gender-affirming care for minors after Trump's administration sent subpoenas and publicly boasted about intimidating providers, leading 17 Democratic attorneys general to file suit on August 1, 2025.

title: RSF Press Freedom Index: US Drops to 57th, Behind Sierra Leone
synopsis: On May 2, 2025, Reporters Without Borders (RSF) published its annual World Press Freedom Index, ranking the United States 57th out of 180 countries — a decline of 2 places from 2024 and 13 places from 2023, placing the US one spot behind Sierra Leone. RSF noted 'an alarming deterioration in press freedom' under Trump's second term and cited 'an authoritarian shift in government,' including weaponized institutions, defunding of independent media, and sidelining of reporters. The US social indicator score dropped 28 places, and the economic indicator fell 14 points over two years. The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) issued a simultaneous warning urging newsrooms to form a united front against the 'rising tide of threats.' The RSF noted that over 60% of journalists surveyed in Arizona, Florida, Nevada, and Pennsylvania said it was 'difficult to earn a living wage as a journalist.'

title: Trump Executive Order Mandates Proof of Citizenship to Register to Vote
synopsis: On March 25, 2025, Trump signed Executive Order 14248, directing the Election Assistance Commission — an independent bipartisan agency — to add documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to the national mail voter registration form. The order threatened to strip federal election funding from any state that refused to comply. An estimated 21.3 million eligible U.S. citizens (9% of voting-age citizens) lack readily available proof of citizenship, including a passport or REAL ID. Multiple federal courts issued preliminary injunctions blocking the order's key provisions; a permanent block on the citizenship-proof mandate was issued October 31, 2025, with a court ruling Trump lacks authority to unilaterally alter election procedures.

title: Trump Threatens to Deploy National Guard to 2026 Midterm Polling Places
synopsis: In a January 7, 2026 New York Times interview, Trump expressed regret that he had not directed the National Guard to seize voting machines after the 2020 election, signaling his intent to use military force around the 2026 midterms. Trump had already deployed the National Guard to at least four Democratic-led cities against the will of their governors in 2025, with courts issuing multiple injunctions. A February 2026 PBS News report revealed a 17-page draft executive order circulating among Trump allies that would declare a national emergency to take federal control over midterm elections, require hand-counting of ballots, and force voters to re-register with proof of citizenship. Trump publicly threatened on Truth Social: 'There will be Voter I.D. for the Midterm Elections, whether approved by Congress or not!' Legal experts said any troop deployment to polls would violate multiple federal statutes.

title: Trump EO Orders Ballots Must Be Received by Election Day, Threatens Funding to States
synopsis: Section 7 of Trump's March 25, 2025 Executive Order 14248 directed the Attorney General to sue any state that counted absentee or mail-in ballots received after Election Day, even if postmarked on or before Election Day — a practice used by millions of voters in numerous states. The EAC was directed to condition federal election funding on states adopting this hard Election Day receipt deadline. A federal judge in Boston issued a preliminary injunction on June 13, 2025, blocking the ballot-deadline provision along with the citizenship registration mandate, ruling Trump lacked authority to mandate changes to state election procedures. At least three states — Kansas, North Dakota, and Utah — separately passed legislation eliminating their mail ballot grace periods following the EO's political pressure.

title: Pentagon Retaliates Against Gen. Milley, Launches IG Investigation
synopsis: On January 29, 2025, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth revoked retired Gen. Mark Milley's personal security detail and suspended his security clearance, ordering the Pentagon Inspector General to investigate Milley's conduct and determine whether his four-star rank should be retroactively stripped. Milley had been on Iranian kill lists since 2020 after Trump's order to kill Qassem Soleimani — leaving him without protection against a documented threat. Senators condemned the revocation as placing Milley and his family in grave danger. Former Chief of Staff John Kelly and former Defense Secretary James Mattis were also subjected to retributive administrative actions, and a federal grand jury indicted John Bolton in October 2025 on charges of unlawful handling of classified information.

title: AG Bondi Creates 'Weaponization Working Group' Targeting Bragg, James, Smith
synopsis: On February 5, 2025, Attorney General Pam Bondi issued a memo titled 'Restoring the Integrity and Credibility of the Department of Justice,' creating a Weaponization Working Group specifically naming Manhattan DA Alvin Bragg, New York AG Letitia James, and former Special Counsel Jack Smith as subjects of investigation. The memo accused the prior DOJ of spending more than $50 million 'targeting' Trump and directed investigators to examine all federal cooperation with New York state legal actions against Trump. By August 2025, DOJ had convened a grand jury and subpoenaed James' office for documents. In October 2025, James was indicted by a Trump-installed loyalist prosecutor; a federal judge dismissed the case in November 2025, finding the prosecutor had been unlawfully appointed.

title: DOJ Drops Police Consent Decrees for Minneapolis, Louisville, Eight Other Cities
synopsis: On May 21, 2025, the DOJ Civil Rights Division — led by Harmeet Dhillon — announced it was dismissing pending lawsuits and proposed consent decrees against the Minneapolis and Louisville police departments, as well as closing investigations into six additional departments: Phoenix, Trenton, Memphis, Mount Vernon (NY), Oklahoma City, and Louisiana State Police. The Minneapolis and Louisville decrees had been negotiated following the police killings of George Floyd and Breonna Taylor respectively. Dhillon characterized the Biden-era investigations as relying on 'flawed methodologies' and 'wrongly equating statistical disparities with intentional discrimination.' Former DOJ Civil Rights Division chief Kristen Clarke called the rollback a 'patent disregard for our laws and the Constitution.'

title: DOJ Directs Investigations Into George Soros-Funded Progressive Prosecutors
synopsis: In May 2025, the DOJ Civil Rights Division opened an investigation into Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty over a policy directing prosecutors to consider racial disparities in plea negotiations. In September 2025, a DOJ senior official directed U.S. attorney's offices in at least seven states to prepare investigations into George Soros' Open Society Foundations on potential charges including material support for terrorism, arson, wire fraud, and racketeering — the directive following Trump and Vance publicly calling for Soros to be investigated. In May 2026, DOJ launched a civil rights probe into Fairfax County Commonwealth Attorney Steve Descano, who received over $600,000 from a Soros-funded PAC, over a policy of weighing immigration consequences in charging decisions.

title: Trump Threatens Insurrection Act Invocation Against Democratic Cities
synopsis: Beginning in October 2025, Trump repeatedly threatened to invoke the Insurrection Act of 1807 to deploy active-duty military troops into Chicago, Portland, and other Democratic-led cities over resistance to ICE operations. A federal judge in California had already ruled in September 2025 that the administration's deployment of active-duty troops to Los Angeles violated the Posse Comitatus Act of 1878. Senior White House aide Stephen Miller had been the leading internal proponent of invoking the Act, and officials shifted from debating whether to invoke it to how and when. Trump described anti-ICE protesters in Portland as committing 'pure insurrection,' while Illinois Gov. Pritzker accused Trump of deliberately manufacturing pretexts for military deployment against his political opponents.

title: Jack Smith Final Report: Evidence Was Sufficient to Convict Trump
synopsis: On January 14, 2025 — six days before Trump's inauguration — the Justice Department released Volume 1 of Special Counsel Jack Smith's 137-page final report on the election subversion investigation. Smith declared unequivocally that 'the admissible evidence was sufficient to obtain and sustain a conviction at trial' and that Trump had engaged in 'criminal efforts to retain power,' making 'specific and knowingly false claims of election fraud.' The report quoted Trump privately remarking after Biden appeared on TV 'Can you believe I lost to this f---ing guy?' and documented Trump berating Pence for being 'too honest.' Smith noted the only reason Trump escaped prosecution was DOJ's longstanding policy against prosecuting a sitting president — not the absence of evidence. Trump dismissed the report as the work of a 'lamebrain prosecutor.'

title: Trump Calls Putin's Ukraine Invasion 'Genius' and 'Savvy'
synopsis: On February 22, 2022, Trump declared on radio: 'I went in yesterday and there was a television screen, and I said, This is genius. Putin declares a big portion of Ukraine as independent.' He praised Putin as 'very savvy' for framing the invasion as a 'peacekeeping' operation. Although pre-dating his second term, the statements directly shaped his second administration's pro-Russia Ukraine posture — he repeatedly cited them in office to justify refusing to condemn Putin, and no retraction was ever issued. Rep. Liz Cheney responded: 'Former President Trump's adulation of Putin today — including calling him a genius — aids our enemies.'

title: Family Separation 2.0: 205,000 Children Lose a Parent to Deportation
synopsis: Unlike the border-based 'zero tolerance' separations of Trump's first term that affected roughly 5,000 children, the second term's family separations played out invisibly across U.S. communities. A July 2025 ICE directive rescinded Biden-era protections against detaining parents of U.S.-citizen children and abolished requirements to place detained parents near their minor children. The Brookings Institution estimated approximately 205,000 children — 71 percent of them U.S. citizens — had a parent detained by immigration officials as of May 2026; CNN identified over 100 U.S.-citizen children left stranded without parents by September 2025. ORR shared over 460,000 tips about unaccompanied children with ICE, leading to more than 12,000 arrests of child sponsors.

title: DOGE Attempts to Access Every American's IRS Tax Records
synopsis: Starting February 16, 2025, DOGE operative Gavin Kliger — a 25-year-old software engineer — arrived at IRS headquarters demanding broad access to a master database containing tax returns, addresses, Social Security numbers, income details, and child custody information for every taxpayer, business, and nonprofit in the country. Senior IRS executives pushed back, describing the request as a worst-case privacy scenario. A February 21 memorandum of understanding ultimately limited access to anonymized data only, after three weeks of internal standoffs. The episode revealed that DOGE had simultaneously deployed Kliger across OPM, USAID, and the State Department, essentially embedding a single operative as a data harvester across the entire federal government.

title: $TRUMP Memecoin Launched 3 Days Before Inauguration — $14B Peak, Suspected Insider Trading
synopsis: On January 17, 2025 — three days before his inauguration — Trump announced $TRUMP, a Solana-based memecoin distributed through Trump Organization affiliates CIC Digital LLC and Fight Fight Fight LLC, which retained 80% of the total 1 billion token supply. The coin's market cap surged to over $14 billion at its peak on January 20. A crypto wallet documented by Wired purchased $1.1 million in tokens within 90 seconds of Trump's announcement before the coin was indexed on exchanges, then made an estimated $85–$116 million in gains — suggesting insider knowledge. More than $2 billion in cumulative losses were suffered by retail investors who bought after the peak, while Trump-affiliated entities profited enormously from the coins they retained.

title: $MELANIA Memecoin Launches Inauguration Eve, Crashes $TRUMP 50% Instantly
synopsis: On January 19, 2025 — the eve of the inauguration — incoming First Lady Melania Trump launched the $MELANIA memecoin via her company MKT World LLC, just two days after Donald Trump's $TRUMP coin. The coin briefly reached a fully diluted market cap of over $5 billion, with the team retaining 35% of the 1 billion token supply on a 13-month unlock schedule. The launch immediately crashed $TRUMP by approximately 50%, from $72 to $44, as traders sold Trump coins to fund Melania purchases. A crypto personality publicly admitted to having known about $MELANIA in advance, and the simultaneous launch of two presidential family memecoins within 48 hours of taking office was condemned by ethics experts and prominent voices within the cryptocurrency industry as 'grifting at the expense of the crypto community.'

title: Musk Uses X to Publicly Expose SSA Data, Implying Fraud Without Evidence
synopsis: In February 2025, Musk posted Social Security Administration data directly on X, sharing figures about beneficiary age distributions drawn from SSA's Numident database — a master file of personally identifiable information for every American with a Social Security number. Musk implied massive fraud by suggesting that people over 100 were collecting benefits, posting: 'Maybe Twilight is real and there are a lot of vampires collecting Social Security.' Former SSA officials publicly explained that the Numident records were simply not updated with death records and had no correlation to actual payment records, calling Musk's interpretation 'just silly' and 'manipulative.' SSA Commissioner Michelle King had already resigned over DOGE's handling of the data; Musk was publicly broadcasting sensitive federal database contents sourced through unauthorized system access to justify further cuts.

title: Big Beautiful Bill Guts Medicaid: 10 Million Lose Coverage
synopsis: Trump signed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act on July 4, 2025, enacting the largest Medicaid rollback since the program's creation. The Congressional Budget Office projected the law would reduce federal Medicaid spending by $793 billion over 10 years and increase the uninsured population by 10.3 million by 2034. Key cuts included work requirements for 18.5 million expansion adults, six-month eligibility redeterminations instead of annual, and the elimination of ACA marketplace subsidies for immigrants. Combined with expiring enhanced ACA premium tax credits, CBO projected 16 million total additional uninsured Americans by 2034.

title: Medicaid Work Requirements Signed Into Law: 5–10 Million Face Disenrollment
synopsis: Section 44141 of the One Big Beautiful Bill, signed July 4, 2025, requires states to enforce 80-hours-per-month work requirements on Medicaid expansion adults beginning January 1, 2027, affecting an estimated 18.5 million enrollees. The Robert Wood Johnson Foundation modeled that between 4.9 and 10.1 million people would lose Medicaid coverage by 2028 depending on state implementation. Nebraska began early implementation on May 1, 2026. The CBO found that 4.8 million of those disenrolled would be working adults who simply fail to navigate complex monthly reporting systems — not people actually violating work requirements.

title: RFK Jr. Promotes Vitamins Over Vaccines During Measles Crisis
synopsis: HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. responded to the worst measles outbreak in 33 years by promoting vitamin A, cod liver oil, budesonide, and the antibiotic clarithromycin as alternatives to vaccination — recommendations doctors called dangerous misinformation. AP News reported that Kennedy had not been briefed in person by CDC infectious disease experts on the outbreak as late as March 21, 2025, weeks after the first child death. In May, Kennedy directed federal health agencies to search for 'new treatments' for measles including vitamins rather than issue a unified call for vaccination. His HHS simultaneously laid off approximately 10,000 federal health workers, disrupting CDC laboratory capacity and the FDA's bird flu testing infrastructure.

title: EPA Proposes Repealing Greenhouse Gas and Mercury Standards for Coal Plants
synopsis: On June 11, 2025, EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced proposals to repeal all greenhouse gas emission standards for power plants under Section 111 of the Clean Air Act and to roll back the 2024 Mercury and Air Toxics Standards, reverting mercury limits to 2012 baselines. EPA simultaneously granted 71 coal-fired power plants two-year exemptions from existing Mercury and Air Toxics Standards, more than any other industrial category. Zeldin called climate action 'a cult' and framed coal power as essential for AI data centers. Environmental groups said weakening mercury rules would increase exposure to a potent neurotoxin that impairs brain development in children across coal-producing and downwind states.

title: BLM Opens 250,000 Wyoming Acres Near Yellowstone and Grand Teton to Oil Drilling
synopsis: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum signed a secretarial order in February 2025 requiring BLM to prioritize reducing barriers to energy development on public lands and shorten permitting timelines from two years to 28 days under emergency procedures. The administration's 2025 Wyoming lease sales offered 45,804 acres near Yellowstone for oil and gas drilling, followed by a proposed 2026 auction of over 250,000 Wyoming acres, including more than 88,000 acres overlapping all three state-designated mule deer migration corridors and the pronghorn corridor adjacent to Grand Teton National Park. The Big Beautiful Bill additionally mandated that at least 50% of all industry-nominated public lands be made available for leasing, removing BLM's conservation-based discretion.

title: Endangered Species Act Protections Stripped from Lesser Prairie Chicken
synopsis: On February 26, 2026, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service formally delisted both population segments of the lesser prairie chicken from the Endangered Species Act, following Trump administration decisions to side with Texas, Oklahoma, and Kansas in lawsuits filed by the beef and petroleum industries. Federal protections had been vacated by a Trump-appointed federal judge in Midland, Texas, in two rulings — for the northern population on March 29, 2025, and for the endangered southern population on August 12, 2025. The delistings benefited the Permian Basin Petroleum Association and National Cattlemen's Beef Association, who argued conservation easements were sufficient, ending requirements for energy companies and ranchers to protect the birds' mating grounds across the southern Great Plains.

title: Trump Media Raises $2.5 Billion from ~50 Institutional Investors for Bitcoin Treasury
synopsis: On May 27, 2025, Trump Media & Technology Group — the parent company of Truth Social, of which Donald Trump owns just over 50 percent — announced it would raise $2.5 billion from approximately 50 institutional investors: $1.5 billion in stock at the last closing price and $1 billion in convertible bonds, to build a Bitcoin Treasury. Trump, as controlling shareholder, stood to directly benefit from any appreciation in DJT stock triggered by the capital raise and Bitcoin strategy. The deal was announced less than two weeks after Trump's Middle East trip, during which Gulf sovereign wealth funds and crypto-adjacent entities were central participants in investment forums. The transaction deepened concerns that Trump's personal financial stake in Truth Social created ongoing incentives to promote crypto-friendly regulation, tax treatment, and foreign investment flows into entities he controlled.
